title: Dynamic Graph World Modelling: Learning Future Dynamics from Temporal Context
abstract: arXiv:2610.19364v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Dynamic graph learning models how entities and their relations evolve from historical observations to predict future graph states. Existing methods do not fully address dynamic graph world modelling, which requires learning transitions from temporal context to future latent graph states. This is difficult for three reasons: nodes and relations rely on different historical evidence, structural evolution is path-dependent, and future snapshots provide sparse and realization-specific targets. We propose Dynamic Graph World Modelling (DyG-WM), the first framework to jointly predict future node and relation representations from temporal context by answering three questions: what has evolved, how it evolved, and what will evolve next. To capture what has evolved, a historical node-relation context encoder summarizes node-neighborhood trajectories and pair-specific histories. To characterize how it evolved, a node-relation path-signature encode

translated_title: 动态图世界建模：从时间上下文中学习未来动态
translated_abstract: 动态图学习通过从历史观测中对实体及其关系的演化进行建模，以预测未来的图状态。现有方法尚未充分解决动态图世界建模问题，即需要学习从时间上下文到未来潜在图状态的转移。这一任务的难点主要有三：节点和关系依赖不同的历史证据，结构演化具有路径依赖性，且未来快照提供的监督目标稀疏并依赖于具体实现。我们提出动态图世界建模，这是首个通过回答三个问题——什么发生了演化、如何发生演化、接下来将演化什么——来从时间上下文中联合预测未来节点与关系表示的框架。为了捕捉“什么发生了演化”，历史节点-关系上下文编码器总结了节点邻域轨迹和节点对特定的历史；为了刻画“如何发生演化”，节点-关系路径签名编码器……
tldr: 提出首个动态图世界建模框架DyG-WM，通过回答“什么演化了、如何演化、接下来将演化什么”三个问题，从时间上下文中联合预测未来的节点与关系表示。
en_tdlr: DyG-WM is the first dynamic graph world modelling framework that jointly predicts future node and relation representations from temporal context by answering three questions: what has evolved, how it evolved, and what will evolve next.
